caption: The drawing depicts the upper portion of a building, with a focus on a detailed brick chimney structure rising above a tiled roof. The chimney is constructed of reddish-brown bricks arranged in a decorative pattern, with diagonal crossings and some horizontal layers, topped by a sloped, tiled cover composed of earth-toned, weathered tiles. The roof immediately below the chimney consists of rows of rounded, clay roof tiles in shades of ochre and brown. The wall beneath the roof is shown with a rough, light beige or off-white plaster surface, featuring a dark irregular patch on the right side, possibly indicating weathering or damage. The background is plain and uncolored, with the entire composition centralized and framed by broad, empty space. There is a small, handwritten inscription near the bottom right of the drawing.
title: Chimney
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
